strategy.summary: Float32 gradient accuracy bug in jax.lax logistic, tanh and expm1 under AccuracyMode.HIGHEST: the buggy JVP rules use ans*(1-ans), (1+tanh)(1-tanh) and expm1+1, which lose accuracy and make the logistic gradient vanish near x~17 instead of ~88; the fix uses ans*logistic(-x), 4*sigmoid(2x)*sigmoid(-2x) and exp(x) under HIGHEST only. The developer test testEvenFunctionGrads (logistic, tanh) and testExpm1Grad in tests/lax_test.py exercise this via jax.vmap(jax.grad(...)) on float32 inputs with accuracy=HIGHEST.

pinned_because: jax and XLA have no documented version constraint and no era ceiling in the evidence, so the strategy uses the jax/jaxlib revision checked out at the buggy commit 1b556f2e7444 (editable install from the repo) rather than a pinned PyPI release; jaxlib must match the source revision's XLA
XLA version is not stated in the evidence and is taken from the jaxlib built or installed with the buggy checkout; no era-inferred pin is applied

strategy.reproducing_test: tests/lax_test.py::LaxTest::testEvenFunctionGrads (parameters logistic, tanh) and tests/lax_test.py::LaxTest::testExpm1Grad, added by PR #30346
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 1b556f2e7444 the added tests FAIL: the grad of logistic/tanh at x and -x (float32, HIGHEST) differ beyond atol from jtu.default_tolerance()[float32] with rtol=0, and expm1 grad differs from exp grad over [-80,80) beyond the same atol. On the fixed revision (the PR head with the logistic/tanh/expm1 JVP changes applied) the same tests PASS.
strategy.numerical_probe: jax.vmap(jax.grad(lambda x: jax.lax.logistic(x, accuracy=jax.lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST)))(jnp.array([20.0, 30.0], dtype=jnp.float32)) — buggy gradient is 0 where the fixed gradient is nonzero
risks: The defect only manifests when accuracy=AccuracyMode.HIGHEST is passed explicitly; default-accuracy runs will pass on both revisions and cannot demonstrate the transition, so the test must set accuracy explicitly.

The evidence gives no numeric threshold at which correct and buggy answers separate beyond the test atol; the transition relies on the test's atol from jtu.default_tolerance() for float32, whose exact value is not stated in the context.

The fix also removes the accuracy argument from logistic_impl, so the forward lowering is unaffected; if the buggy revision already differs in forward path, failures could come from elsewhere, which should be checked against the diff.

Platform, backend (CPU vs GPU/TPU) and XLA fusion behaviour are not stated; the vanishing gradient is a float32 arithmetic effect that may differ across backends, so a run on a backend other than the one where the defect was observed may not transition.
No sanitiser or architecture-specific behaviour is evidenced, but the test is a float32 accuracy check and results depend on XLA's exp/expm1/logistic implementations, which are not pinned here.
Repository-level test setup (jtu, parameterized) must be importable from the checkout; the test file also contains an unrelated whitespace removal, which is harmless.

oracle.reference_source: the test's own comparison: grad at x vs -x for logistic/tanh (even-function symmetry), and exp grad for expm1
oracle.why: Mathematically the gradients of logistic and tanh are even functions and expm1's gradient equals exp, so the test compares against those identities at the stated float32 tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the logistic gradient ans*(1-ans) saturates to 0 for x>~17 at float32 while the value at -x does not, so the assertAllClose on grads vs neg_grads exceeds atol; likewise expm1+1 for large negative x and (1+tanh)(1-tanh) for large x diverge from their references, so the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With ans*logistic(-x) for logistic, 4*sigmoid(2x)*sigmoid(-2x) for tanh and exp(x) for expm1 under HIGHEST, the gradients agree with their references within atol, so the assertions pass.
